puzzles.description: Raja — Chief Architect. Short dialog, three exchanges max. Gives you the FSM engine cue and later releases the Composer's Studio gate.

config.name: Raja
config.greeting: You made it. The pipeline is stuck. The FSM engine keeps requesting directives but the state file is corrupted. I need you to restart the engine sequence — properly, with the audit hooks on. No shortcuts. No skipped human gate.

lines.label: Walk me through the engine.
lines.response: Ten canonical steps. Human sends intent. Conductor reads skill. Conductor invokes FSM. FSM reads graph. FSM reads state. FSM returns directive. Persona hat or sub-agent takes the directive. Human gate for high-judgment. Report. Dispatch again. Audit hooks fire throughout — that's non-negotiable.

lines.label: Why does the state file matter?
lines.response: The FSM is deterministic. Give it the graph and the state, it returns the next directive without spending an LLM token on routing. Without the state, it loops. That's why we're stuck. Restart it. Toggle the state machine on, toggle the audit hooks on, type the output word, and leave the human gate ALONE.

lines.label: What's next after the engine's back?
lines.response: Two things I need you to bring me — in parallel, using sub-agents. The verification-key from the Inner Loop, and memory.md from the Memory Vault. Bring both back here and I'll open the Composer's Studio. Then we right-size the workflow and ship.

state_lines.label: I've got the verification-key.
state_lines.response: Good. Inner loop's back. Still waiting on the memory rules. Send someone to the vault before the state file finishes decaying.

state_lines.label: memory.md is here.
state_lines.response: Both back? Then click 'Report back to Raja' and I'll open the Composer's Studio. That Golem is trying to run 32 stages for a typo fix — go strip it down before it hallucinates something worse.

state_lines.label: The orchestra played.
state_lines.response: I saw. Fourteen stages, twenty-three minutes, two human gates. That's the pipeline as it was designed. Go watch the release. Then loop back and encode what we learned — so tomorrow's Conductor is faster than you were.

The answer is CONDUCTOR.

puzzles.description: Restart the FSM engine under a 90-second timer — toggles ON where required, do NOT skip the human gate, and type the FSM's output word.
hints: State Machine ON, Audit Hooks ON, Read Graph and Read State both ON. Skip Human Gate is a TRAP — leave it OFF. Type the word the FSM returns.
The FSM's output — the thing it returns after reading graph and state — is the DIRECTIVE. Type that in the code field.
State Machine=ON, Audit Hooks=ON, Read Graph=ON, Read State=ON, Skip Human Gate=OFF, code=DIRECTIVE.

puzzles.description: Route the seven agents to their correct phase of the AI-DLC V2 workflow.

components.label: Product Manager
components.hint: Captures user intent — turns 'we need X' into a spec.

components.label: Systems Architect
components.hint: Chooses the pattern and defines boundaries before code starts.

components.label: Adaptive Composer
components.hint: Scores complexity and proposes the right-sized workflow.

components.label: Security Reviewer
components.hint: Runs SAST and inspects for policy violations at build time.

components.label: QA Engineer
components.hint: Runs tests and verifies traceability against requirements.

components.label: SRE
components.hint: Owns deploy, monitoring, and rollback in production.

falseOutputs.pm->construction: PM captures intent — that happens before construction. Ideation.
falseOutputs.pm->operation: PM isn't running the deploy — they set the intent up front.
falseOutputs.arch->construction: Architecture is decided in Inception, before code generation begins.
falseOutputs.arch->ideation: Architects consume intent, not produce it. Inception.
falseOutputs.composer->construction: The Composer scores the workflow BEFORE construction begins. Inception.
falseOutputs.composer->operation: Composer is upstream of building — not downstream of shipping.
falseOutputs.dev->ideation: Developers turn a spec into code — that's the build phase, not the intent phase.
falseOutputs.dev->operation: Developer generates the artifact. Operation is about running it.
falseOutputs.sec->operation: Security Reviewer catches issues at build time. Runtime security is SRE's world.
falseOutputs.sec->ideation: Security review happens against the artifact — that's Construction.
falseOutputs.qa->ideation: QA can't verify what hasn't been built. Construction.
falseOutputs.qa->operation: QA verifies the artifact before it ships. Operation is what happens after.
falseOutputs.sre->construction: SREs come in at deploy and after — Operation.

config.successMessage: All seven agents routed to their correct phase.

hints: Ideation captures intent (PM). Inception designs the shape (Architect, Composer). Construction builds and verifies (Developer, Security Reviewer, QA). Operation ships and runs (SRE).
Only one agent lives in Ideation — the one who turns raw intent into a spec. Two live in Inception — the ones who choose the shape and score the workflow.
PM→Ideation. Arch+Composer→Inception. Dev+Sec+QA→Construction. SRE→Operation.

puzzles.description: Wager on your confidence about V2 self-verification. Bigger stakes, bigger reward — and bigger penalty on a wrong answer.

questions.question: What happens when the inner loop's iteration budget expires?
options: Restarts the whole workflow from stage 1

questions.question: Which verification type checks coding standards and traceability?
Which verification type runs linters and SAST?
options: Both, but the LLM is authoritative

questions.question: What breaks the inner loop BESIDES the iteration budget?
options: The models cannot reconcile their outputs
The linter runs out of memory
A new agent is added to the pipeline
questions.answer: The models cannot reconcile their outputs

questions.question: Who can always override the QA agent's verdict?
options: Whichever agent has the highest confidence score

hints: V2's escape hatch is always the same: when the AI can't decide, the human decides. That's the whole point of the outer loop.
Inferential = 'does an LLM think this reads right' (quality, traceability, standards). Deterministic = 'does a tool say YES/NO' (linter, SAST, tests).
Answers: outer loop, Inferential, Deterministic, models can't reconcile, the human always overrides.

You have a 1000-token capacity. intent-capture (200) + code-generation (400) + unit-test (300) = 900. Perfect.
Load: intent-capture.md, code-generation.md, unit-test.md. Reject: requirements-analysis, application-design, security-review, mockups, arch-diagram, load-test-plan.

puzzles.description: Eight rapid-fire decisions. 12 seconds each. Wrong or timeout resets the streak.

questions.question: Intent captured. What's the next FSM directive?
decoys: Skip ideation — go straight to code

questions.question: Models can't agree on the fix. Escalate?
decoys: No — ship both and A/B test

questions.question: Human approves. Record learning?
decoys: Save to the LLM's context only

questions.question: Same mistake seen before. What does memory say?
decoys: Fork the rule for this project

questions.question: All stages complete. Hook action?
decoys: Skip hooks — they slow us down

hints: Every answer matches what the pipeline was designed to do: FSM directs, AI verifies AI, human paged only on deadlock, memory encoded per scope, hooks always fire, deploy is the endpoint.
When in doubt: pick the option that trusts the loop. The wrong answers are all shortcuts, escalations, or bypasses.
In order: Begin ideation, QA Reviewer, Inner loop self-corrects, Yes — human outer loop, project.md, Apply existing rule, Write audit event, Deploy to production.

puzzles.description: Approve the pipeline replay — one wrong approval breaks the chain. Five learnings, five decisions.

steps.question: Bottleneck Shift — The Conductor delegated code generation to a sub-agent. The verification agent found a linting error and fixed it autonomously. No human was paged.
options: Page the human reviewer — we need sign-off on everything
Inner loop self-corrected. Low-judgment work ships without human.
Delete the linting rule — it's too strict

wrong.0: This is the old bottleneck! The whole point is that AI verifies AI for low-judgment work.
wrong.2: The linter caught a real violation. Deterministic checks exist for a reason.

steps.after: ✓ Learning 1: AI verifies AI. Humans engage only for high-judgment decisions.

steps.question: Deterministic FSM — The state machine advanced from inception to construction. It read the stage graph, found code-generation next, and issued the directive. No tokens spent on routing.
options: The LLM should decide what stage comes next — it's smarter
Deterministic engine drives progression. LLM energy saved for generation and verification.
Skip the state machine — just let agents figure it out

wrong.0: Using LLM for routing wastes tokens on decisions a simple program can make. That's V1 thinking.
wrong.2: Without the FSM, agents have no guaranteed execution order. Chaos — not autonomy.

steps.after: ✓ Learning 2: Deterministic tools drive workflow. LLMs reserved for knowledge work.

steps.question: Memory Compounds — A developer corrected a coding convention. The system asked: 'Memorize this?' They said yes. Next project, the same convention was applied automatically.
options: Memory is nice but I'll just re-explain next time
Save to project.md. It applies next iteration — effort descends.
Save everything to org.md — one file for all rules

wrong.0: Re-explaining is the plateau! The whole point is: teach once, never re-explain. Effort descends.
wrong.2: Memory is hierarchical. Project rules in project.md, org rules in org.md. Don't pollute the layers.

steps.after: ✓ Learning 3: Corrections become durable rules. The system learns — effort descends over time.

steps.question: Adaptive Composition — The Composer analyzed the bug fix: low ambiguity, high test coverage, small code change. It proposed 3 stages instead of 32.
options: Always run all 32 stages — thoroughness matters
Right-sized to 3 stages. No bloat, no debt. Ship fast with confidence.
Skip all stages — just commit directly

wrong.0: 32 stages for a typo fix is stage bloat. The AI forces itself to produce output for stages that don't need it — hallucinations follow.
wrong.2: Zero stages means zero verification. You'll ship bugs. The Composer finds the minimum viable workflow.

steps.after: ✓ Learning 4: Adaptive composition right-sizes the workflow to the problem.

steps.question: The Conductor Ships — Jakarta's MRT digital signage update deployed. 14 stages. 23 minutes. 2 human gates. 11 specialist agents. 1 Conductor. Zero gridlock.
options: The Conductor managed everything alone — no agents needed
The Conductor orchestrated. Specialists did their jobs. Humans elevated to judgment. The macet is cleared.
Agents are unreliable — go back to manual

wrong.0: The Conductor doesn't do the work — it delegates to specialists. That's the orchestra model.
wrong.2: Manual is the old gridlock. The pipeline shipped in 23 minutes. A human team would have taken days.

steps.after: ✓ Learning 5: The Conductor orchestrates an orchestra of agents. Humans elevated. Gridlock cleared. Macet selesai.

onComplete.text: The Jakarta MRT glows green. Every station name correct. Every digital sign alive.
onComplete.subtext: The pipeline learned from today. Tomorrow — fewer stages, fewer gates, faster delivery. Macet selesai.

hints: Every step is the same choice at heart: trust the loop over the shortcut. AI verifies AI. FSM drives. Memory scopes. Composer right-sizes. Conductor orchestrates.
Wrong answers are all traps that look reasonable: page the human on everything, let the LLM route, don't record memory, always run all stages, do it manually.
In order: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1. The middle option, every time.
